parts.title: Practical Learning In The Classroom
parts.article:
A The way we think about architecture in schools has come along way. Once, studying architecture in the art class meant learning to appreciate great buildings art-history style, through slide presentations. In recent years, though, the American Institute of Architects has fostered the idea that the process of architectural design, not just the appreciation of architecture, is a beneficial aspect of the art curriculum (Sadler, 1989).

B The value of architectural design is that it is the concrete training ground for a broadly applicable creative process. Architectural training can help people design structures to meet needs. It can help farmers design crop rotations to meet needs. Furthermore, it provides hands-on experiences that reinforce learning in various other subjects, from math to social studies.

C In the ongoing dialogue about architecture in the middle school art curriculum, many believe students should actually build the structures they design in their courses. Although the technology and expertise required of modern architecture can prohibit students from actually realizing their designs, traditional architectural materials and methods remain quite accessible to the art classroom. Traditional architectural materials, such as earth, clay and straw, are cheap, easy to work with and readily available. Further, when students participate in the construction or preservation of a traditional earthen structure in their local community, they engage in a form of experiential learning and they are motivated to invest in the project. This is evident in a case study of an adobe* conservation project with middle school students in the town of Zuni, New Mexico, in the Southwestern United States.

D Traditional architecture reaches back to preindustrial America, when local resources and cultures produced structures in styles unique to each region. In New Mexico, examples of hand-built earthen structures still abound. The region has seen some decline in traditional architecture as industrialization has brought new building codes and materials; however, the traditional, non-industrial home, either preserved from earlier generations or newly built, remains in use. Traditional building materials and the land that supplies them are so accessible that handcrafting a house still remains feasible.

E Thus, with no technical expertise and little cost, middle school students can participate in the construction or preservation of a traditional earthen structure. During the project, a student will get to know the materials, understand the chemistry, solve problems, work with classmates, and exercise muscles. The student can apply knowledge of design principles and the creative process while participating in a cooperative effort. But most significantly, this type of project-based activity motivates students to invest intellectually and emotionally in the outcome.

F The town of Zuni, where I taught art, was surrounded by adobe construction, new and old. Behind our main high school building there was a one-room adobe structure which was once used for teaching. Now it served as a place where old furniture could be kept. I sent my class home with the oral history assignment to ask their family, friends and neighbors questions to find out about that building. From their research we compiled a sketchy history: it began as a kindergarten classroom; it later became an art classroom; now it was full of broken desks.

G The building's design kept it relatively warm in the winter, even without heating, due to its broad south face, and it stayed cool in the summer due to its spacious, ventilated attic and massive earthen walls. Because of this, my students agreed it was worth preserving and were enthusiastic about helping. Preservationist Shalie Gasper arrived in the fall to help with an assessment of the building's needs. She recommended replacing the stucco** that encased the original adobe walls with a traditional mud plaster. She showed us where to find local supplies of sand and clay soil for the plaster mix. We began work on the stucco removal in late fall. The next spring the students were ready to replaster. To teach the traditional skills, Gasper and other local specialists joined us. They gave my class three full mornings of intensive workshops on history and preservation as well as mud-plastering technique, and the building got a new coat of traditional mud plaster.

H Small design-and-build projects such as this can be seen through to the finish when working with earth in the art curriculum. A simple landscape feature such as a wall, entryway, or arch can draw students into important aspects of design that involve the structure's interaction with people, the surrounding landscape, and natural elements. The same project may provide an opportunity to focus on the chemistry of soil or the structural dynamics of construction. Design goals might guide students to involve traditional forms, consider formal aspects, or integrate math skills of measuring and estimating.

I During our traditional architecture unit, the students realized that something old and almost forgotten is valuable and worth preserving. Many others in the community and around the country share this renewal of interest in traditional earthen technologies. It is the connection to a cultural heritage that interests some; the quality of living within massive, natural walls that attracts others; or for others, the sustainability of the process and the minimal energy spent in construction. The value of adobe in general is becoming more and more known, but little has been said about its value in the art curriculum until now. This experiment in adobe conservation with middle school students convinced me that traditional architecture deserves a place in the regular curriculum.
parts.questions:
Questions 27–31
Choose the correct letter.

Q27 What education initiative does the American Institute of Architects currently promote?

  • A multimedia presentation of information in classrooms
  • B the study of monumental buildings throughout history
  • C the practice of designing architectural structures
  • D processes to add more art classes in schools

Q28 In the third paragraph, what problem with teaching architecture on art courses does the writer note?

  • A Technology-based courses are unavailable.
  • B Students cannot always construct their designs.
  • C The curriculum is too traditional.
  • D Students lack motivation.

Q29 What is the greatest benefit for students that the writer sees in a traditional architecture project?

  • A personal connection to the end result
  • B participation in a cooperative project
  • C building of problem-solving skills
  • D conservation of a traditional building

Q30 What is the purpose of the eighth paragraph?

  • A to explain why it is important that projects be small
  • B to outline the multiple skills involved in one project
  • C to discuss strategies for connecting content areas
  • D to propose suggestions for traditional earth projects

Q31 What does the writer say about traditional building and the general population?

  • A Earthen architecture is becoming a profitable business.
  • B Earthen architecture is less feasible in some areas of the country.
  • C Interest in earthen architecture varies from region to region.
  • D People are attracted to earthen architecture for different reasons.
Questions 32–36
Complete the summary using the list of words, A-H, below.
Write the correct letter in boxes 32-36.
The students in Zuni chose to renovate an old building which was being used for . They came to an agreement that the building was worthy of rehabilitation based on its functional . At the beginning of the project, students were given the task to discover the history of the building through interviews with local residents. Through the course of the project, they learned where to locate for the project. They also worked closely with a number of on each step of the project. During the project, students were also given to build useful skills.
  • A experts
  • B location
  • C design
  • D storage
  • E students
  • F resources
  • G training
  • H businesses
Questions 37–40
Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer?
In boxes 37–40 on your answer sheet, write:

Q37 The price of materials is one drawback to using traditional architecture.

  • A YES
  • B NO
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q38 Earthen structures can easily be built in all regions of the U.S.

  • A YES
  • B NO
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q39 Working with a traditional earthen structure can have physical benefits.

  • A YES
  • B NO
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q40 A traditional architecture curriculum is best suited to middle school level students.

  • A YES
  • B NO
  • C NOT GIVEN

reference:
Q27

解析 原文明确提到美国建筑师协会提倡将“建筑设计的过程”作为艺术课程的有益部分，也就是让你去动手实践设计。

干扰 你可能想选B，因为第一句提到了欣赏伟大建筑，但这描述的是以前的做法，而不是目前协会倡导的。

句子 In recent years, though, the American Institute of Architects has fostered the idea that the process of architectural design, not just the appreciation of architecture, is a beneficial aspect of the art curriculum (Sadler, 1989).

Q28

解析 原文指出，现代建筑所需的科技和专业知识会让学生无法真正把设计建造出来（realizing their designs）。

干扰 你可能想选A，但原文是说现代建筑对技术有门槛要求，而不是说学校里缺乏基于技术的课程。

句子 In the ongoing dialogue about architecture in the middle school art curriculum, many believe students should actually build the structures they design in their courses. Although the technology and expertise required of modern architecture can prohibit students from actually realizing their designs, traditional architectural materials and methods remain quite accessible to the art classroom.

Q29

解析 作者认为最重要的一点（most significantly）是，这类项目能激发学生在智力和情感上对结果的投入，也就是对最终成果产生了个人情感连结。

干扰 你可能想选B或C，因为原文确实提到了合作和解决问题，但它们并不是作者强调的“最大（most significantly）”益处。

句子 The student can apply knowledge of design principles and the creative process while participating in a cooperative effort. But most significantly, this type of project-based activity motivates students to invest intellectually and emotionally in the outcome.

Q30

解析 第八段列举了一个建筑项目如何让学生接触到化学、结构动力学以及数学等多种知识，目的是讨论如何把不同学科内容结合起来。

干扰 你可能会选B，虽然确实提到了不同的技能，但整段的核心目的在于展示一个项目如何跨界将多个学科领域的知识串联在一起。

句子 Small design-and-build projects such as this can be seen through to the finish when working with earth in the art curriculum. A simple landscape feature such as a wall, entryway, or arch can draw students into important aspects of design that involve the structure's interaction with people, the surrounding landscape, and natural elements. The same project may provide an opportunity to focus on the chemistry of soil or the structural dynamics of construction. Design goals might guide students to involve traditional forms, consider formal aspects, or integrate math skills of measuring and estimating.

Q31

解析 原文明确列举了人们对传统土建感兴趣的多种原因，有人因为文化遗产，有人因为生活质量，还有人因为环保可持续性。

干扰 你可能想选C，但原文是说“有些人”因为这个原因，“另一些人”因为那个原因，并没有说兴趣是根据“地区”来划分的。

句子 Many others in the community and around the country share this renewal of interest in traditional earthen technologies. It is the connection to a cultural heritage that interests some; the quality of living within massive, natural walls that attracts others; or for others, the sustainability of the process and the minimal energy spent in construction.

Q32

解析 原文说这个老建筑现在被用来存放旧家具，直接对应了选项中的“储物（storage）”。

干扰 你可能看到“teaching”想选学校相关的词，但题目问的是“正在被用来（was being used for）”做什么，应该对应原文的“现在（Now）”的作用。

句子 Behind our main high school building there was a one-room adobe structure which was once used for teaching. Now it served as a place where old furniture could be kept.

Q33

解析 原文提到是因为建筑的“设计（design）”让它冬暖夏凉，所以学生们因此（Because of this）一致认为它值得修复。

干扰 你可能会漫无目的地去前面找原因，但“值得修复（worth preserving）”的直接原因就是紧挨着的前一句所描述的功能性设计。

句子 The building's design kept it relatively warm in the winter, even without heating, due to its broad south face, and it stayed cool in the summer due to its spacious, ventilated attic and massive earthen walls. Because of this, my students agreed it was worth preserving and were enthusiastic about helping.

Q34

解析 原文说专家告诉他们去哪里找沙子和粘土这些“物资（supplies）”，同义替换就是选项中的“资源（resources）”。

干扰 你可能想选B（location），但题目里已经有“where to locate（去哪里找）”了，填location会导致语义重复。

句子 She showed us where to find local supplies of sand and clay soil for the plaster mix.

Q35

解析 原文提到有当地的“专家（specialists）”加入进来，完美同义替换选项中的“专家（experts）”。

干扰 你可能会因为前面一直在说学生，而误选E（students），但题目问的是在各个步骤上“与谁密切合作”，指的是这些外来的专业人士。

句子 To teach the traditional skills, Gasper and other local specialists joined us.

Q36

解析 原文提到专家为了教技能，给学生上了三个早上的“密集工坊课（intensive workshops）”，这就属于一种技能“培训（training）”。

干扰 你可能会去生搬硬套原文里的具体词汇，但这里考查的是对“intensive workshops”的概括理解。

句子 To teach the traditional skills, Gasper and other local specialists joined us. They gave my class three full mornings of intensive workshops on history and preservation as well as mud-plastering technique, and the building got a new coat of traditional mud plaster.

Q37

解析 原文明确说传统建筑材料“很便宜（cheap）”，所以价格不仅不是缺点（drawback），反而是优点。

干扰 你可能看到“drawback”就潜意识觉得土建肯定有缺点，但没有回原文去核对价格这个具体信息。

句子 Traditional architectural materials, such as earth, clay and straw, are cheap, easy to work with and readily available.

Q38

解析 原文只提到了新墨西哥州有很多这种建筑，完全没有提及是不是美国“所有地区（all regions）”都能“轻松”建造。

干扰 你可能因为原文提到了“unique to each region（每个地区独有）”就觉得是NO，但原文并没有评价“其他所有地区”好不好建，属于信息缺失。

句子 Traditional architecture reaches back to preindustrial America, when local resources and cultures produced structures in styles unique to each region. In New Mexico, examples of hand-built earthen structures still abound. The region has seen some decline in traditional architecture as industrialization has brought new building codes and materials; however, the traditional, non-industrial home, either preserved from earlier generations or newly built, remains in use.

Q39

解析 原文提到参与这个项目可以“锻炼肌肉（exercise muscles）”，这直接印证了题目所说的“身体上的益处（physical benefits）”。

干扰 你可能会过度关注前面的化学和解决问题等脑力活动，而漏看了半句结尾处的“锻炼肌肉”。

句子 During the project, a student will get to know the materials, understand the chemistry, solve problems, work with classmates, and exercise muscles.

Q40

解析 原文只说了和“初中生（middle school students）”的实验让作者确信传统建筑应该加入常规课程，但并没有和其他年龄段比较，没说“最适合（best suited）”初中生。

干扰 你可能会因为通篇都在拿初中生举例子，就理所当然地认为这是“最适合”他们的，忽略了比较级（best suited）在原文中是不存在的。

句子 The value of adobe in general is becoming more and more known, but little has been said about its value in the art curriculum until now. This experiment in adobe conservation with middle school students convinced me that traditional architecture deserves a place in the regular curriculum.
